protocols.summary: Take an idea, from three words to a short paragraph, through the software delivery cycle (docs/phases.md).

Fix one reported bug in an existing code tree, red first: the bug report is dissected into a checked data document, a test that reproduces the bug is written and observed failing on the unchanged code while the rest of the suite passes, and only then is the fix admissible; the same test and the whole suite must pass on the fixed revision, the bug's story is moved to implemented, and the code tree's gate (build, test, lint, format) passes.
Fix the project context, the vision and the roadmap (docs/phases.md steps 4 to 6).
Deliver one epic of the approved roadmap (docs/phases.md steps 7 to 10).
Turn an idea into a requirements list (docs/phases.md steps 1 to 3).
Decompose the epic's complete ESS specification into AEP stories under the epic.

Release and operate the result of a specification whose stories are delivered: build a release with provenance, run the ESS conformance suite of the current specification revision against it, publish it on a person's approval, and observe it running.
Get the epic's ESS specification to complete (docs/phases.md steps 8 and 9).

Deliver one AEP story of an approved ESS specification: implement it against the current specification revision, verify it with the ESS conformance run against the implementation, have it reviewed, once that run passed, by a principal other than its implementer, and merge it once a person with the merge authority approved that change revision.

limits: **No evaluation run was made on this code.** The three runs of record `experiments/parity-loom-strong-4.yaml` ran on the code of 0.6.0 and delivered 0 of 3; all stopped `stuck`. Two of the causes the record names are not fixed in this release. A model node that is not called (a finding waits for a person, or the decisions it would follow are the defaults) exits 0 and still counts against `budget.max_runs` at Loom `db2726ff` (run 1 stopped at `spec.author`, run 3 at `change.implement`; `bindings/PENDING.md` names the missing not-called exit of the bindings). And a rejection gives the writer no new allowance of runs: the cycles `decider-rework-spent` and `rework-fresh-allowance` still fail on `RunsSpent` (`docs/cycles-suite.md`). The cause of run 2 (an action dated by the next `evaluated` line) is what `db2726ff` changes; a no-model test (`runbook/tests/test_suite/amend.rs`) holds that state and a run of it ends `passed`, but no evaluation run has used it.

**No statement about speed, quality or cost goes beyond `experiments/`.** The release claims no measured change over 0.6.0 or over the old driver; a figure in these notes is one that a record of `experiments/` carries or a count read from the tree.

**The old driver's records keep its names.** Records of past runs (`cases/**/evidence`, `experiments/`, the recorded run of `ui/test/recorded/`) keep the producer id `sdc-drive`, and the record `parity-loom-strong-4` names files that are deleted now.

**The cycles are not all converted.** Of the 130 entries of the old suite 40 are converted, 14 are pending, 39 are held by Rust tests and 37 are dropped. The whole file is a slow lane, `task test:cycles-loom`; it was not run on this tree for this note, and `docs/cycles-suite.md` says that cycles run at a one-minute load of 100 to 177 ended on Loom's 60 s wall bound (11 entries). The replay entries are Rust tests of the slow lane `task test:replay`, not run for this note either.

**`sdc-experiment` does not carry an effort.** It refuses `efforts.*` in a `loom` variant: the record format does not carry an effort to the runner yet, so the class defaults apply to a run it starts. `sdc-node --effort` and the settings file of `runbook run` do carry one.

**The daemon runs a stub unless asked.** `runbook serve` runs the stub runtime, in which nothing is executed, unless `--runtime loom` is given (`runbook/src/serve.rs`, `docs/engine.md`); the daemon's default confinement floor is `linux` and `local` must be asked for by name (`docs/daemon-api.md`). The Loom runtime is run through the slow lane `task test:engine-real`, not by the gate.

**`--confinement local` is unconfined.** `local` is "unconfined and declared insecure" (`docs/loom-run.md`): a bound program can write the whole run directory, including the copy of the routing table (the runner reads it once, so a rewrite changes no routing), the decider's instruction files and adapter, and the replay plan and call log. Under `--confinement substrate` the run directory is out of a bound program's reach (`docs/loom-run-decisions.md`).

The rule approver (`SDC_RULE_APPROVALS`, claims of the position), the rework cap of the old driver and the end by rule `withhold` are not in the runner: Loom's output holds no claim values and Loom has no such steps (`docs/loom-run-decisions.md`).

`task check:ess-suite:slow`, the byte comparison of a new synthesis with the committed suite, and `task docs:test` were not run for this release; the fast digest check is part of `task check:ess-generated`.
